image_prompt.text: A river wide enough for a group to float down together, flowing between two low shores that run alongside it the whole way
Slush blops standing along both shores at varied distances back from the water, arranged so a player drifting past can read which ones are in range
A rack of water guns at the launch dock where players pick one up before getting in the water
An upstream launch dock where players and their friends get into the river together, set back far enough that the first blops are out of range
A takeout beach at the downstream end where the float finishes and the payoff sits

layout_placement.text: Blop positions along both banks, gradeable by distance from the water so range varies as the player drifts past
Pick-up and swap point for the water gun at the launch dock
Group spawn on the upstream dock, outside the range of the first shoreline blops
End-of-run zone on the downstream takeout beach

mechanics: you float down the river with your friends
you use water guns to shoot
the current carries the player downstream rather than the player walking
slush blops are the things being shot at
notes: preset Aim Trainer kept, but its shape range-directed was substituted for route-guided: range-directed states there is no route through the space, and here the player travels the whole length of the space while shooting sideways off it.
route-guided is not in Shooter's typical shapes; taken from shapes.md. route-point-to-point was rejected because nothing in the prompt makes the float a timed run, and it would have added P6.
pipeline CHECK comes only from water-body. The play volume is a surface float down an open channel, so self-occlusion is unlikely; the rest of the build is P0.
traversal is water-borne — players are carried by the current, not walking — so walkability and jump-gap assumptions do not read as usual.
the place the run ends was inferred, not stated: winner-zone as a downstream takeout beach.
the launch point was inferred from the scene. Shooter has no plain shared-spawn row (only opposing team bases and a spawn shield), so spawn-protected was bent into an upstream dock.
scale band assumed: the individual blops argue for room detail, the length of a river argues for more extent; block was taken as the compromise and the prompt named no extent.
theme emitted null per layout-intake's rule even though 'slush blops' and water guns read strongly toon.

Do the slush blops just sit on the bank as things to shoot, or do they keep coming — appearing somewhere onshore and moving toward the water? Fixed positions and spawn points are built differently.
Is there an end to the river — a beach or dock where the float finishes — or does it loop round so you can keep drifting?
Nothing was said about how this should look. Bright and cartoony like a water park, a natural forest river, or something else you had in mind?

skill_gap.name: water as traversal medium
skill_gap.why: the river is both the route and the surface the player travels on, and no shape carries water. route-guided had to hold the route while the universal water-body — worded as a scenery feature and routed CHECK — had to hold the water, so the prompt's central geometry is split across two picks and the whole build's only modifier comes from a row that was not meant to be load-bearing. The bank alongside it has no row at all.

notes_for_us: options.md has no Type column, so a cross-genre layout pick (winner-zone) cannot fill layout_placement.type without loading the owning genre file the read scope excludes.

Emit says P0 is dropped once any modifier is present, but CHECK is a flag rather than a route. SET has an explicit 'keeps P0 alongside' exception and CHECK does not, so this build emits ['CHECK'] and reads as if it has no baseline route.

layout-intake says to infer theme from the prompt where possible and then says to emit null and never guess when the prompt is silent; a prompt whose vocabulary is toon but which states no theme falls between the two rules.
The pilot prompts.json has no 'enriched' field, so coverage.enriched_invented cannot be filled as LANE-BRIEF describes.
Shooter's table has no plain shared spawn — only opposing team bases and a spawn shield — so an ordinary 'everyone starts here together' point has to be bent out of spawn-protected.
